Key observations from test image:
- Soybean stems near/at soil line
- Dark brown to black lesion/canker on lower stem
- Dead/dying plant material
- Some orange-reddish coloration at base
- Plants appear dead or near-dead

Top candidates: Phytophthora, Charcoal_Rot, Anthracnose, White_Mold, Rhizoctonia

Now I have enough reference images. Let me synthesize my analysis.

**Test Image Analysis:**
- Mature soybean plants (pods visible, late season)
- Very dark, blackened/decayed stem mass at/near soil line
- Surrounding plants are dead and dry
- Orange-reddish coloration visible at base
- Appears to be a stem-base/root crown disease

**Comparison Results:**
- **Phytophthora**: Reference top-left shows dead soybean plants with dark chocolate-brown lower stem, very similar overall field appearance to test image
- **SDS**: Bottom-left reference shows dark rotted root mass; but SDS typically shows interveinal chlorosis and blue fungal growth
- **Charcoal Rot**: Gray/bleached stems with marbled interior — doesn't match the dark solid mass
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown lesion near soil; reference shows reddish-orange stem coloration
- **Fusarium**: Dark rotted root mass with cortical decay — somewhat similar but usually shows brown vascular tissue

**Key distinguishing feature**: The central dark brown-black stem lesion beginning at soil line, with completely dead plants (leaves/pods still attached to dead stems), most closely matches **Phytophthora** — the hallmark symptom of which is dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward, with plants dying and leaves remaining attached.
